hops.rationale: Within MSFT's fiscal 2024 10-K (accession 000095017024087843), the passages cover both requested elements. Passages 46 and 47 describe competition in cloud-based services, including competitors' cloud models, pricing pressure, and AI competition. Passage 47 states MSFT is "incurring significant costs to build and maintain infrastructure to support cloud computing and AI services" and that these costs will reduce operating margins. Passage 96 says cloud and AI infrastructure will increase operating costs and may decrease operating margins, and describes datacenter expansion and its inputs. Passage 102 adds Microsoft Cloud gross margin commentary tied to scaling AI infrastructure, and passage 185 gives Intelligent Cloud segment revenue and operating income. No dedicated quantified breakdown of cloud infrastructure operating costs appears, but the goal did not require one, so core facts are supported. The AMZN comparison is outside this scope and was not graded.

The passages cover the operating-cost side well: AWS net sales of $90,757M and operating expenses of $66,126M for 2023 (up from $57,255M in 2022), AWS operating income of $24,631M, and that AWS income growth was partly offset by payroll and technology infrastructure spending to support AWS growth.
